task: Build a workspace with a git dependency, or audit a workspace's dependencies, under strong source pins
do: Run `blaze audit pin` at the workspace root. It fetches each git source's tree fresh, hashes it, and writes `[git."<url>"] <commit> = "blake3:..."` into blaze.lock. Review the printed digests and the file's diff, then commit it. To audit, clone https://github.com/rustsec/advisory-db somewhere, set `[workspace.metadata.blaze.audit] database = "<dir>"` (or BLAZE_AUDIT_DB), run `blaze audit pin` again to pin the database's tree, then run `blaze audit` (or `--json`, with `--today YYYY-MM-DD` for a reproducible report). Accept a known finding with `accept = [{ id = "RUSTSEC-...", reason = "...", until = "YYYY-MM-DD" }]`. All the logic is in crates/blaze-audit (sans-IO, tests in src/tests.rs); the drivers are crates/blaze-cargo/src/cli/audit.rs, blaze-units load/source.rs (`require_git`) and blaze-cargo serve/fetch/git.rs (`verify_git`).
why: A commit id is SHA-1, which is no pin: a git dependency whose tree digest blaze.lock does not record is refused at load (rule `weak_source_pin`), and a fetched tree that differs from its pin is refused before it is mounted. The advisory database is a pinned input too, so its tree must match before it is parsed. docs/v2/plan/design/audit.md has the formats and the threat model.
